d.d: To lay upon, as an order or command; to give an injunction to; to direct with authority; to order; to charge.
To prescribe under authority; to ordain.
To prohibit or restrain by a judicial order or decree; to put an injunction on.
simple past and past participle of enjoin
To receive pleasure or satisfaction from something.
d.x: Enjoy your holidays! I very much enjoy dancing.

d.d: To have the use or benefit of something.
d.x: I plan to go travelling while I still enjoy good health.

d.d: To be satisfied or receive pleasure; to have fun.

d.x: That was an enjoyable day; I had a lot of fun.

d.d: simple past and past participle of enjoy
present participle and gerund of enjoy

d.x: Few activities better the enjoyment of a hearty meal eaten in good company.

d.d: An enjoyable state of mind; a feeling of satisfaction or delight from a situation.
d.x: I experienced more enjoyment from summer camp than any part of school.

d.d: third-person singular simple present indicative of enjoy
